subject: Northbridge next steps — eval criteria, pin/rollback thresholds
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
To: Simon Kerr <simon.kerr@northbridgeanalytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-05-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + demo — quick recap and proposed next steps

Hi Simon — great chat this morning. Thanks for walking through the three primary workflows (customer support triage, policy classification, and agent summarization). Per our discussion, I wanted to capture the concrete next steps and propose a narrow evaluation plan so we can give you a reliable recommendation and guardrails for any model changes.

Summary of what we agreed: 
- Scope: 1) triage (intent classification + routing), 2) policy classifier (safety labels), 3) summarization (3-sentence resolution summary).
- Data: you agreed to provide ~500 representative examples and 5 golden prompts for each workflow.
- Timeline: initial eval pack back to you in 3 business days; canary plan to follow if results look good.

What we will deliver in the eval pack (attached): 
- prompt_set_v1.jsonl (sample prompts + injection tests)
- benchmark_summary.csv (R1 metrics across candidate models)
- northbridge_eval_pack.zip (raw test harness, seed data, scripts)

Model recommendations (initial): 
- For triage/classification: open-llama-70b-q4f (fast, quant-friendly) and redwood-compat-7b (lower cost fallback).
- For summarization: redwood-summarize-13b (better coherence on long contexts) with a trimmed context window.

Quality/regression note (important): Redwood is scheduled to push runtime model version updates next week in our hosted catalog (minor kernel and tokenization changes). To avoid surprises, we suggest the following conservative policy for Northbridge: pin the serving model to the specific model artifact used for the eval (model_id + checksum), and require a regression window check before any catalog-wide switch. Operational options: 
1) Pin the model for the trial period (recommended).
2) Allow canaryed updates with traffic split (we can roll out 5% -> 25% -> 100% and compare metrics).
3) Auto-rollback trigger if classification F1 drops by >3 pts or summarization ROUGE-L drops by >2.

Ask: Please confirm which option you prefer (pin, canary, or allow catalog updates) and whether procurement should include a pinning SLA in the contract. If you're OK, I'll loop Aditya to enumerate the exact artifact checksums and the rollback playbook.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Enterprise AE — Redwood Inference
phone: (415) 555-0198

Attachments: northbridge_eval_pack.zip (see prompt_set_v1.jsonl, benchmark_summary.csv)
From: Simon Kerr <simon.kerr@northbridgeanalytics.com>

1) On pinning: we prefer to pin during the pilot but are open to a canary approach provided we get daily metric snapshots and an SLA-backed rollback window.
2) For canary thresholds: is the >3pts F1 / >2 ROUGE-L recommendation based on typical observed variance, or is that conservative for a financial/regulatory dataset?

Also looping procurement (procurement@northbridgeanalytics.com) so they can start scoping contract language around pinning and a rollback SLA.

On Tue, May 12, 2028 at 09:12 AM Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Summary of what we agreed...

Hi all — quick tech follow-up from me with proposed acceptance tests and rollback logic.

Acceptance checks (automated):
- Classification: micro/macro F1, precision on safety classes, confusion matrix snapshot for top 5 classes. Baseline pass if relative drop <= 3 pts vs eval artifact.
- Summarization: ROUGE-L, BERTScore, and a small human spot-check sample (10 items). Baseline pass if ROUGE-L drop <= 2 and BERTScore drop <= 0.015.
- Latency: p50/p95 token latencies; fail if p95 increases > 30% from eval artifact during canary.

Pinning/serving details:
- We can pin to model artifact id + semantic checksum (we'll produce model_meta.json in the eval pack). Example id: redwood-summarize-13b@20280512-7f3a2c.
- Canary plan: start 5% traffic for 24h, compare metrics; expand to 25% for 24h; full if no regressions detected.
- Auto-rollback: if any critical metric breaches (classification F1, ROUGE-L, or p95 latency), we trigger an automated rollback and create a ticket in Redwood Console; we'll also notify your SRE contact via PagerDuty if you provide an escalation alias.

I'll attach a lightweight script (included in northbridge_eval_pack.zip) that computes the deltas and flags fails — this is what we'll run during the canary.

Aditya Rao
Principal SE — Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: benchmark_summary.csv, prompt_set_v1.jsonl
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>

Thanks — procurement note: if you want pinning as a contract item, we typically add a clause that defines the pinned artifact and the duration of the pin (e.g., pinned for the pilot + 30 days after go-live) and an exception process for security patches. I'll draft sample language for your counsel (procurement@northbridgeanalytics.com).

Also we'll include a 30-day credits SLA for rollback-triggered incidents during pilot. Simon, if you can confirm the budget owner, I'll surface this in the deal so finance knows to reserve a small contingency.

Marissa Cole
Customer Success — Redwood Inference

- Failure thresholds: use Aditya's acceptance checks; procurement to include a 30-day rollback credits clause.
